threads.response: Fixed reentrant observer shutdown and made stop idempotent. The regression calls stop directly from changed; the original sanitizer reproduction crashed at the ACK write. Callback lifetime and shutdown cases now run in the normal and instrumented observer suite.

No framing change: the relay deliberately requires EOF within its single bounded input/delivery deadline. Returning nonempty input at the deadline still reaches the caller's expired-deadline check and cannot deliver it. Existing kept-open-input coverage verifies a silent, bounded exit. No supported Claude payload was shown to violate this EOF contract.

Retained strict validation. Silently deleting a non-string identity field can change exact request identity into an advisory event. Malformed authenticated metadata intentionally reports observation loss; the current adapter tests cover malformed/oversized events. A future upstream schema needs live qualification and explicit per-field semantics, not silent field removal.

Fixed: stable_notice now explicitly rejects a missing notice before indexing it. The new regression requires the useful observation-loss diagnostic rather than TypeError. It does not wait for a disappeared notice to return or hide the failure.
Removed the redundant --ui-preview arguments from both Claude rejection cases. The shared invocation still supplies it once and the expected rejection messages remain checked.
The launch rejection now names all three conflicting switches: --settings, --bare and --safe-mode. Rejection and literal-argument handling remain unchanged.

Fixed: well-formed unsupported Claude decisions receive a terminal-only diagnostic without detaching the client. Exact pending source/epoch/request/revision matches receive the existing correlated retry frame; stale/malformed control messages retain their guards. No answer reaches Claude. The live hook probe submits a rejected decision and verifies the exact token, unchanged pending request and retained attachment.

No null-guard workaround added: the selected state and observer are constructed together, and current shutdown stops rather than independently resets either member. Construction failure unwinds before publication. This proposed partial-teardown state is not reachable in the current lifecycle. Adapter/service lifecycle coverage remains in the validation scope.
Separated the null-preview case from the reconnect-only guard and removed the redundant live_ condition after the guard. The reconnect-only diagnostic now describes only that state.

Fixed the direct begin() guard to call report(), since fail() intentionally returns when already failed. A focused regression exercises both forbidden modes, checks their diagnostic, and confirms the queued reconnect still uses the original trusted identity.

Canonical export is intentional: persisted endpoints and duplicate checks use the same resolved endpoint identity. Documented the canonical-path contract. The live-connection fixture now canonicalizes its expected endpoint rather than hardcoding the macOS /private/tmp alias.

Kept the internal manifest's canonical lowercase encoding and clarified both its diagnostic and documentation. The writer already emits lowercase and no other supported writer contract was established. The strict round-trip check continues to reject ignored/noncanonical input rather than accepting fromHex's permissive parsing.

Fixed by separating trusted-directory canonicalization from socket-only validation. The registry no longer probes a fake registry.guard socket or inherits sun_path limits. Regression cases cover a deep valid registry directory and an unrelated regular guard file. Real service socket paths retain their platform limits; the redundant initial storage-path assignment is removed.
Lock failures now distinguish actual contention from other system errors and handle EINTR without relabeling it as another writer. Exclusive locking and trusted-file validation remain enforced.

Consolidated existing-file validation while preserving the exists-or-isSymLink guard and corruption check. The offered exists-only hunk would skip dangling symlinks; the regression now covers that case. Endpoint normalization is consolidated safely rather than simply removing validation.

The asserted never-finishing future is not reproduced. The installed Qt QPromise destructor calls cancelAndFinish(); the focused runtime probe reports finished=1 and canceled=1 after destruction without finish(). Current operations already encode ordinary errors in their result. The proposed catch-all can instead deliver no result to consumers that call result(), so it was not applied.

Added an explicit Retry saving workspace action. Failed saves still freeze registry mutations and surface the error; after correcting the cause, one retry uses the normal validated atomic-write path. Tests cover repeated failure, refusing corrupt contents, successful recovery after repair, and preservation of a live shell. No automatic retry loop or corruption overwrite was introduced.

Removed the /private/tmp fixture assumption and canonicalized the actual temporary directory when constructing its expected endpoint. This preserves macOS identity equality without requiring the macOS alias on other systems. Verified on macOS; Linux UI remains explicitly deferred.
Hoisted the shared eligibility predicate. enabled still additionally requires response choices, preserving terminal-only notices that deserve attention but cannot be answered in the desktop.

Centralized the C++ interaction-block reason constants and exposed the modal reason to QML through the existing UiPreview object. The QML setter and C++ cleanup now consume the same key. Existing modal, pointer/touch, held-key and focus tests remain the behavioral coverage.

Renamed the signal to holdingKeysChanged atomically across Q_PROPERTY, declaration, connects and emits. The old explicit NOTIFY binding was functional; this completes the naming cleanup without leaving stale references.
Removed the unused headers and macOS process-header block from the attention probe. The affected target is compiled; existing identity and cleanup assertions are preserved.

Removed the write-only SourceRecord role and endpoint fields and their initializer arguments. SourceConfig/verified session identity validation remains intact; no redundant assertions were added just to consume dead fields.
Duplicate of discussion_r4076675687: the same SourceRecord fields and initializer are removed in that single cleanup, with identity assertions preserved.
Removed the write-only SessionRecord endpoint field and initializer argument. Cleanup still obtains current endpoints from the live sessions, and process/session identity checks remain intact.
